title: Recovering signatures of archaic hominin introgression using ancestral recombination graphs.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Zenodo record 19685110 ('Trace_data', CC-BY-4.0, 2026-04-21) holds exactly one file, trace_zenodo.tar.gz, 1,761.2 MB. I range-downloaded the first 47 MB, unpacked the readable prefix and opened real files: 5 window-frequency CSVs (12,200 / 17,000 / 14,200 / 22,000 / 11,100 rows; columns chr,start,end,nea_50k,den_50k,ghost_50k,nea_100k,den_100k,ghost_100k), two peak BED files (628 Ghost and 26 Neanderthal peaks in Africans, 216 haplotypes), nine treeID sample tables (216 West-African, 198 East-African, 398 European, 400 East-Asian, 400 South-Asian, 398 Oceanian haplotypes), archaic_deserts.tsv, and the deposit READMEs. I also listed both GitHub repositories (YulinZhang9806/trace, a pip-installable hidden Markov model package with one 2.1 MB example tree sequence; YulinZhang9806/trace_paper, Snakemake pipelines) and read the bioRxiv preprint full text (PMC12991142).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Row counts of the per-haplotype tract tables in data/tables/ (they sit past the 47 MB prefix I read and the whole archive is 1.76 GB, over the 50 MB rule), the reported precision (~90%) and false discovery rate (<0.25%) on simulated SINGER-inferred ancestral recombination graphs, the per-population ancestry percentages, and the statement that >90% of Neanderthal and 70% of Denisovan TRACE segments overlap hmmix or IBDmix calls.

a1_downloadable.note: Open Zenodo deposit, CC-BY-4.0, no login; but it is a single 1,761 MB tar.gz, over the project's 50 MB cap, so I could only read it by ranged requests.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: A label column exists: assign_label (NEA/DEN/Ghost) in the tract tables per the README, and per-window ancestry frequencies (nea_50k, den_50k, ghost_50k) in the CSVs I opened.

a3_inputs_present.note: FAIL: the model inputs are not in the deposit. The inferred ancestral recombination graphs (tree sequences from SINGER) and the genotypes are absent; only one 2.1 MB toy tree sequence exists on GitHub. You would re-run genome-wide ARG inference on 1000 Genomes, and the Oceanian genomes (Choin et al. 2021) are not in this deposit.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are clear in the files I opened: base-pair coordinates (hg38), centimorgans, frequencies in 0-1, haplotype counts; READMEs document every column.

a5_enough_rows.note: Verified 76,500 one-kilobase windows across the 5 region CSVs, plus 628+26 peak intervals; per-haplotype tract tables are larger but their row count is unverified.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 1.76 GB compressed archive; individual raw tsv members up to 99 MB; re-deriving inputs needs genome-wide SINGER ARG inference
a6_fits_laptop.note: The tables alone would fit, but any model that takes genomic input requires re-running SINGER ancestral recombination graph inference over ~2,500 genomes, which is cluster-scale, not laptop-scale.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Everything I could check lines up: 216 haplotypes in the African peak files matches the 216-line West-African treeID table; no contradictions found, but tract-table counts were unverifiable.

a8_label_provenance.note: FAIL and fatal: every label here (assign_label, mean_posterior, window ancestry frequency) is the output of TRACE's own hidden Markov model run on inferred ancestral recombination graphs. No physical measurement of archaic ancestry exists for a haplotype, and for 'ghost' ancestry no archaic genome exists at all, so a supervised model would be distilling TRACE with no way to know where it is wrong.

existing_models.name: TRACE (this paper; hidden Markov model over ancestral recombination graph features, pip-installable at github.com/YulinZhang9806/trace)
existing_models.score_and_split: Paper text: ~90% precision and <0.25% false discovery rate on simulated data with SINGER-inferred ancestral recombination graphs, with much lower recall than on true simulated graphs; evaluated on held-out simulations, not on any measured truth set.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Recall drops sharply when graphs are inferred rather than known, and ghost-ancestry calls cannot be validated because no ghost archaic genome exists.

existing_models.name: ArchIE (Durvasula & Sankararaman 2019, PLOS Genetics; logistic regression on population-genetic summary statistics, github.com/sriramlab/ArchIE), with a 2024 successor ArchIE2
existing_models.score_and_split: Precision-recall and ROC curves on coalescent simulations of a 2% Neanderthal admixture human demography; trained and tested on simulations.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Reference-free calling of ancestry from unknown ('ghost') archaic sources, and robustness to demographic misspecification.

existing_models.name: IntroUNET (Ray, Flagel & Schrider 2024, PLOS Genetics; U-Net image-segmentation neural network on genotype matrices, github.com/SchriderLab/introNets)
existing_models.score_and_split: High per-allele accuracy on simulations including bidirectional gene flow, plus application to Drosophila simulans/sechellia; simulation-trained, simulation-tested.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Transfer from simulated to real data and sensitivity to the assumed demographic model.

existing_models.name: genomatnn (Gower et al. 2021, eLife; convolutional neural network on genotype matrices for adaptive introgression, github.com/grahamgower/genomatnn)
existing_models.score_and_split: Trained on SLiM/stdpopsim simulations; pretrained models and human predictions shipped in the repository; evaluated on held-out simulations.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Distinguishing adaptive introgression from selection on standing variation, and dependence on simulated training distributions.

existing_models.name: Benchmarks that already exist: an MBE 2026 comparison of 11 Neanderthal-introgression callers (admixfrog, ArchaicSeeker2, ArchIE, ARGweaver-D, CRF, DICAL-ADMIX, hmmix, IBDmix, SARGE, Sprime, S*) and a 2026 reliability study of SPrime/IBDmix/hmmix/cp-archaic
existing_models.score_and_split: The reliability study reports F1 of 0.92-0.94 for cp-archaic on three simulation settings and under 22% agreement between methods on real 1000 Genomes data.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Methods disagree strongly at the individual-genome level; there is no measured ground truth in real data.

backbone.name: Nucleotide Transformer or HyenaDNA (DNA language models) would fit a window-level sequence task; no backbone exists for ancestral recombination graphs
backbone.hardware: CPU for embedding a few tens of thousands of 1 kb windows; GPU for anything genome-wide
backbone.licence: Data is CC-BY-4.0; backbone licences permissive to non-commercial

integration.partner_dataset: hg38 genomic annotations already shipped in the deposit (GENCODE v49 protein-coding BED, 1000 Genomes strict mask) plus external recombination maps or the AlphaGenome variant-effect atlas
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do sequence or regulatory features predict where archaic ancestry is depleted, i.e. are 'ancestry deserts' explained by function rather than chance? - a real question, but one that can only be asked against an inferred ancestry map, not a measured one.

controls.positive_control: A model should recover the known Neanderthal-ancestry depletion on chromosome X and in the five classical desert regions (chr1 98-115 Mb, chr3 76-90 Mb, chr7 106.5-128.5 Mb, chr8 54.4-65.5 Mb, chr13 48.9-61.1 Mb), all present in the files I opened.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle window labels within chromosome and confirm collapse to the genome-wide mean frequency.
controls.external_validation: Published Neanderthal ancestry maps (Sprime, IBDmix, hmmix) exist as a second source, but they are other inference methods, not independent measurements, and the 2026 benchmark reports under 22% site-level agreement between them.

honest_claim_h3: A model trained here could only claim: 'given hg38 sequence and annotation, I predict the archaic-ancestry frequency that TRACE's hidden Markov model assigned to this window in these 1000 Genomes samples' - a statement about TRACE's output, not about archaic ancestry.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use DNA sequence and genome annotation to predict how much archaic human ancestry each window of the genome carries today.
plain_idea.train_on: One-kilobase windows of the human reference genome with sequence and annotation features; I verified 76,500 such windows with ancestry frequencies in the five deposited region files, and genome-wide arrays exist inside the 1.76 GB archive but their size is unverified.
plain_idea.predict: The frequency of Neanderthal, Denisovan or unknown 'ghost' ancestry in that window. The true answer comes from TRACE, a hidden Markov model run on ancestral recombination graphs inferred from present-day genomes - an inference, not a measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Human-evolution groups would like to know whether ancestry deserts are explained by gene content or sequence features; but because the answer key is one method's output, a good score would only show the model imitates that method.

more_or_better_data.why: TRACE's calls cover 1000 Genomes plus Oceanians, the same panels ArchIE, IntroUNET and the 11-method MBE 2026 benchmark already work on; the deposit adds a new inference, not new measurements.

confidence_score.why: The tables carry a mean posterior probability per segment, so uncertainty exists - but it is the hidden Markov model's own confidence, which TRACE already reports, so a new model would add nothing.

models_beatable.why: TRACE itself is 2026, open-source and evaluated on simulations with ground truth; IntroUNET (2024) and genomatnn (2021) are open with pretrained weights; there is no weak, closed incumbent to displace.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No new data joins here that measures the same quantity: archaic ancestry per haplotype is never measured directly, so the condition 'new data measures the same quantity the same way' fails outright.

ml_idea: The project considered was: predict per-window archaic ancestry frequency (Neanderthal, Denisovan, ghost) from hg38 sequence and annotation with a frozen DNA language model plus a regression head, then ask whether ancestry deserts are predictable from function. It dies because the target is TRACE's own hidden Markov model output, so the model would learn a method, not biology, and for ghost ancestry there is no reference genome anywhere on earth to check it against.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: unpacking the 1.76 GB archive plus annotation joins on roughly 3 million one-kilobase windows would stay under about 4 GB of RAM if processed chromosome by chromosome; embedding hours assume a small DNA language model on CPU over a subsampled window set.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Ask where a single label came from: the deposit README states every tract label is TRACE's assign_label with its hidden Markov model posterior, and the only comparison columns are hmmix and IBDmix - also model outputs. That is a five-minute read and it kills the project.

verdict_reason: Fails A8 and A3. Every label in the deposit - assign_label, mean posterior, window ancestry frequency - is the output of TRACE's own hidden Markov model run on inferred ancestral recombination graphs, with no measured ground truth anywhere (for 'ghost' ancestry no archaic genome exists at all), so any supervised model would distill TRACE and could never be shown to be right. The inputs that would make a genuine model are also absent: no tree sequences and no genotypes are deposited, only post-processed tract tables, so reproducing inputs means cluster-scale SINGER inference over ~2,500 genomes. The field is additionally well served by open, simulation-validated models (ArchIE, IntroUNET, genomatnn) and two 2026 benchmarks. The deposit is nevertheless clean and well documented - CC-BY-4.0, 76,500 verified one-kilobase windows with documented columns - so it is a fine figure-reproduction resource, just not an ML training set.
